content.text:
I've built `/work/spec.vl.json`. It renders with no errors or warnings. It answers the question with **no**: from 2012/13 to 2018/19 every season peaked in ISO weeks 5–9 (February). After 2020 the peak moved around:

| Season | Peak week |
|---|---|
| 2019/20 | W12 |
| 2020/21 | W39 |
| 2021/22 | W11 |
| 2022/23 | W50 |
| 2023/24 | W50 |
| 2024/25 | W07 |
| 2025/26 | W06 |

The figure has a circular view (left) and the full series on a time axis (right). Dragging across the right-hand chart colours the matching weeks in the circle and greys out the rest. I could not drag in the renderer, so I tested the link with a preset selection (mid-2022 to mid-2024). The right weeks lit up, and that test exposed a bug that I fixed: the year colours and legend changed with the selection.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - x/y computed from angle = 2π(week-1)/weeks-in-ISO-year, W1 at top, clockwise; radius = incidence
  R2: done - one line per ISO year, colour (turbo scheme) + "ISO year" legend
  R3: done - max week per Saison marked with outlined point + season label (also marked in linear view)
  R4: done - line of full series 2012-W40 to 2026-W43 on UTC time axis
  R5: done - x-interval brush in linear view; circle shows selected weeks in colour, rest grey; peak markers dimmed
  R6: done - W1, W5, … labels around circle, value rings 1,000–4,000 "per 100,000 / week", year ticks + titled y axis
  R7: done - title + one-sentence caption (subtitle), plus source line
assumptions:
  - Date of an ISO week = its Monday, computed in UTC inside the spec
  - Angle uses 52 or 53 weeks according to the ISO year, so each year makes one full turn
  - Radius has an inner hole (0 = 12% of the radius) so low values stay readable; ring scale max = max value rounded up to the next 1,000
  - Peak colour = the ISO year of the peak week; ties would mark all tied weeks
  - With no brush, all years are shown in colour
limitations:
  - 2026/27 is incomplete (to 2026-W43); its "peak" is marked with a triangle as "season in progress"
  - Lines are not joined across the year boundary (W52/53 → W1), so each ring has a small gap at the top
  - Season labels near the February cluster overlap; the tooltips give the exact season and week
  - Before 2020 the caption's pattern is clear; after 2020 the peak timing varies (W50 to W12, and W39 in 2020/21)
```
